paragraphs: Friend, this is a tough passage, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Paul writes to the church in Corinth about covering the head when praying or prophesying, and he cares about it enough to say, "If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God." (1 Corinthians 11:16) I'll be honest, I'd have a hard time with some of these lines too. But I'm not going to smooth them over or make up a reason Paul never gave.

Here's what I can say for sure: Paul's instruction is that a man prays or prophesies with his head uncovered, and a woman does it with her head covered. (1 Corinthians 11:4-7) He ties it to the order of the heads, Christ, man, woman, and God as the head of Christ, and he points to creation, the angels, and nature itself. (1 Corinthians 11:3, 7-10, 14-15) He also tells them to "Judge for yourselves," so he's asking them to think it through, not just nod along. (1 Corinthians 11:13)

And right in the middle, Paul says "HOWEVER," and then, "In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman." (1 Corinthians 11:11) Then he zooms out: "But everything comes from God." (1 Corinthians 11:12) So, baker, here's what to carry out of the bakery: when you come to pray, come in a way that honors God, and treat the people beside you as people you can't do without, because everything comes from Him. Take your questions about the hard parts to Him, keep reading, and keep your oven ready.
